report_name: New Zealand Report: China is Top State-Sponsored Cyber Threat

threat_actors.name: China
threat_actors.description: Identified by New Zealand's NCSC as the 'most persistent and capable' state-sponsored cyber threat. Conducts long-term espionage campaigns for intelligence gathering, targeting critical sectors in New Zealand such as government, healthcare, and IT.
threat_actors.goals: Intelligence gathering and long-term strategic advantage.

threat_actors.name: Iran
threat_actors.description: Mentioned in the NCSC report as a state actor conducting cyber activities against New Zealand, though at a lesser scale and sophistication than China.

threat_actors.name: North Korea
threat_actors.description: Mentioned in the NCSC report as a state actor conducting cyber activities against New Zealand, though at a lesser scale and sophistication than China.

threat_actors.name: Russia
threat_actors.description: Mentioned in the NCSC report as a state actor conducting cyber activities against New Zealand, though at a lesser scale and sophistication than China.

attack_patterns.name: Search Open Websites/Domains
attack_patterns.description: Used for extensive open-source intelligence (OSINT) gathering to identify key personnel and infrastructure as part of reconnaissance efforts.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: Used as a common entry vector in sophisticated spearphishing campaigns to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Used as a common entry vector to gain initial access to target networks.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Service
attack_patterns.description: Used to establish persistence by creating new services to ensure long-term access.

attack_patterns.name: Scheduled Task
attack_patterns.description: Used as a persistence mechanism to ensure long-term access to compromised systems.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: Used to harvest credentials from the operating system to facilitate lateral movement.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Data is compressed, encrypted, and exfiltrated over common protocols like HTTPS to blend in with normal network traffic.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: Actors utilize living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) as part of a 'low-and-slow' approach to maintain stealth.

indicators.name: Suspicious LOLBin Execution for Ingress
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Certutil Execution For File Download
id: 2b9a4f8e-1c7d-4b0a-9e6f-3d2a1c8b9e0d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of certutil.exe, a living-off-the-land binary (LOLBin), to download files from a remote URL, a common TTP for state-sponsored actors.
references:
  - https://ipdefenseforum.com/2026/10/china-biggest-state-backed-cyber-threat-to-new-zealand-security-agency-says/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1105
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\certutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-urlcache'
      - '-split'
      - '-f'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) for malicious execution, based on patterns observed in state-sponsored campaigns.

indicators.name: Anomalous Interactive Logon by Service Account
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Interactive Logon by Service Account
id: 5e8f1c7d-4b0a-4f8e-9e6f-1c8b9e0d2a9b
status: experimental
description: Detects an interactive logon (Logon Type 2) by a service account, which is highly anomalous and may indicate credential compromise and misuse.
references:
  - https://ipdefenseforum.com/2026/10/china-biggest-state-backed-cyber-threat-to-new-zealand-security-agency-says/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
  - attack.t1003
  - attack.t1078
level: medium
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 2
    AccountName|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects anomalous service account usage, such as interactive logons, which could indicate the use of compromised credentials.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Interactive Logon by Service Account
